title: Ammoron Requests an Exchange
summary: Ammoron sent Moroni a request to exchange prisoners. Moroni rejoiced at the request, desiring provisions for his people and prisoners to strengthen his army.

explicit_facts.text: At the commencement of the twenty-ninth year of the judges, Ammoron sent Moroni a request to exchange prisoners.
Moroni rejoiced at the request because he wanted provisions for his people and prisoners to strengthen his army.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the contents of Ammoron’s request beyond the exchange request stated.

title: Moroni Resolves on a Stratagem
summary: The Lamanites had taken women and children, while Moroni’s prisoners included none. Moroni resolved to obtain Nephite prisoners from the Lamanites and sent Ammoron an epistle by Ammoron’s servant.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites had taken many women and children; Moroni’s prisoners included no women or children.
Moroni resolved on a stratagem to obtain Nephite prisoners from the Lamanites.
Moroni wrote Ammoron an epistle and sent it by Ammoron’s servant, who had brought an earlier epistle to Moroni.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni writes a letter and gives it to Ammoron’s servant to carry.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether any prisoners are visible

narration.text: Moroni resolved upon a stratagem to obtain as many prisoners of the Nephites from the Lamanites as it were possible.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the stratagem succeeding in this scene.

title: Moroni’s Epistle: The War
summary: In his epistle, Moroni addresses Ammoron about the war, warns of God’s justice, and urges him to repent and withdraw his armies to the land of Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni’s epistle addresses Ammoron about the war waged against Moroni’s people and urges him to repent and withdraw his armies to the land of Nephi.
Moroni writes that Ammoron and his brother have been murderers and urges Ammoron to repent and return with his armies to their own lands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni’s words may be shown as off-screen speech over a setting where the letter is being written.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, Ammoron, I have written unto you somewhat concerning this war which ye have waged against my people,

title: Moroni Predicts Ammoron’s Response
summary: Moroni says he expects Ammoron to reject his words again, declares that his people are prepared, and threatens that Nephite armies will defend their cities, lands, religion, and cause.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni expects Ammoron to reject his words again because Ammoron has previously rejected them and fought against the people of the Lord.
Moroni says his people are prepared and that their armies will come against Ammoron if he does not withdraw.
Moroni says the Nephites will retain their cities and lands and maintain their religion and the cause of their God.

title: Moroni Sets Exchange Terms
summary: Moroni says he will exchange prisoners only if Ammoron delivers a man, his wife, and his children for each prisoner. Otherwise, Moroni threatens to fight, declares his anger, and closes by identifying himself as a Nephite leader.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says he will exchange prisoners only if Ammoron delivers a man, his wife, and his children for one prisoner.
Moroni threatens to fight Ammoron, arm his women and children, pursue him into his land, and continue until Ammoron’s people are destroyed.
Moroni says he and his people are angry and that they have sought to defend themselves and their land.
Moroni closes his epistle and identifies himself as a leader of the Nephites.

title: Ammoron Receives the Epistle
summary: Ammoron received Moroni’s epistle, became angry, and wrote back. He identifies himself as king of the Lamanites, says he is Amalickiah’s brother, and threatens to avenge Amalickiah’s blood.

explicit_facts.text: Ammoron received Moroni’s epistle, became angry, and wrote another epistle to Moroni.
Ammoron identifies himself as king of the Lamanites and Amalickiah’s brother, and threatens to avenge Amalickiah’s blood.
Ammoron says he will come against Moroni with his armies and does not fear Moroni’s threats.

title: A Claim to Government
summary: An unidentified speaker accuses the addressees' fathers of taking their brethren's right to government, offers to end the war if the addressees lay down their arms and submit to those the speaker considers rightful rulers, and says the speaker's people do not fear the addressees' threats.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker claims the addressees' fathers took their brethren's right to government.
The speaker offers to have the speaker's people lay down their weapons and end the war if the addressees lay down their arms and submit to those the speaker says should govern.
The speaker says the speaker's people do not fear the addressees' threats.

title: Ammoron Agrees to Exchange Prisoners
summary: Ammoron agrees to exchange prisoners according to Moroni’s request, saying he wants to preserve food for his men of war. He declares that the war will continue until the Nephites submit or are extinguished.

explicit_facts.text: Ammoron agrees to exchange prisoners according to Moroni’s request to preserve food for his men of war.
Ammoron says the war will continue until the Nephites submit to Lamanite authority or are extinguished.

title: Ammoron’s Response About God
summary: In his epistle, Ammoron says he does not know the God Moroni says he has rejected. He also questions the existence of a devil and hell and dismisses the matter.

explicit_facts.text: Ammoron says he and the Nephites do not know the being Moroni calls God, and says that if such a being exists, he may have made both peoples.
Ammoron raises the possibility of a devil and hell and says these things do not matter.

title: Ammoron’s Ancestry and Purpose
summary: Ammoron identifies himself as a descendant of Zoram and a bold Lamanite. He says the war has been waged to avenge past wrongs and obtain and maintain rights to government, then closes his epistle to Moroni.

explicit_facts.text: Ammoron says he is a descendant of Zoram, whom Moroni’s fathers pressed and brought out of Jerusalem.
Ammoron calls himself a bold Lamanite and says the war is to avenge wrongs and obtain and maintain rights to government.
Ammoron closes his epistle to Moroni.
